newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Albright, Cohen for foreign team.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Albright, Cohen for foreign team.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday chose U.N. Ambassador Madeleine Albright as the first woman secretary of state in U.S. history and decided on a Republican, William Cohen, as defence secretary, White House officials said.

Rounding out his national security team for his second term, Clinton decided to nominate presidential National Security Adviser Anthony Lake as Central Intelligence Agency director and replace Lake with his deputy, Samuel Berger.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton would announce his new national security team in an Oval Office ceremony at 1:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT). All the posts, except national security adviser, require Senate confirmation.
Aides said Albright was offered the job by Clinton in a telephone call Thursday.
The selections followed a protracted period of deliberation by Clinton, who was re-elected on November 5, as he sought to form a national security team that could work well together.
He settled on Albright to replace Warren Christopher after considering a number of other candidates, including former Maine Senator George Mitchell and former Bosnian special envoy Richard Holbrooke.

Cohen's selection marks a fulfilment of a promise by Clinton to put a Republican in his Cabinet. The Maine senator is a 24-year veteran of Congress, where he gained an expertise in defence affairs. He is a published poet and spy novelist.

Lake, 57, would replace John Deutch as director of the Central Intelligence Agency and other arms of the massive American spy apparatus. Deutch, who had been considered a candidate to replace Perry, was expected to return to private life.

Lake, a cerebral gentleman farmer from Massachusetts, has been at Clinton's side throughout all his foreign policy decisions over the past four years. Many in the White House believed the CIA is suited for Lake because he shies away from a public role.

His long-time deputy national security adviser, 51-year-old Berger, is seen by many White House aides as an able replacement for Lake. He is said to have a keen political sense and will be more media savvy than Lake.
